newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ELECTIONS SEEN ON TIME DESPITE FLOOD.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ELECTIONS SEEN ON TIME DESPITE FLOOD.

text.p: Prospects that Poland's general elections, due on Spetember 21, will be put off due to July's flood waned on Friday as the co-ruling Peasant Party decided against supporting a motion to declare a state of emergency.

The right-wing and centrist opposition demanded that the state of emergency be imposed in the south and west of the country to help the authorities fight the worst flood in centuries, which would automatically postpone the vote.

Some Peasant officials earlier said they favoured delaying the polls, but the party leadership decided on Friday it would not back the opposition's parliamentary motion asking the president to launch the special measure.
"The state of emergency is a thing of the past, because the flood is going away," Peasant leader Waldemar Pawlak told a news conference.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski, the only person authorised by law to declare the state of emergency, has also said he was against the move unless the deluge returns.

The biggest party in the ruling coalition, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), has always abjected to delaying the polls, in which they hope to defeat its main challenger, the Solidarity Election Action alliance (AWS).
